lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 -- The Patient Journey
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Graziele Dias | Lesson 21 -- The Patient Journey
lesson.grammar_point: sequencing words (first, then, next, after that, finally)

listenings.text: Hi Graziele, this is Doctor Carter. Thank you for today. I have a small request. Tomorrow, three doctors from Toronto visit your hospital. Could you present the patient process to them? Please say it step by step. First, the admission. Then, the exam. After that, the result. Finally, the discharge. Short and clear. See you tomorrow.

Hi Graziele, it is Ana. A quick tip for your presentation. Use small words to show the order. For the first step, say first. In the middle, say then, next, or after that. For the last step, say finally. Put one step in each sentence, and make a small pause after each order word. Keep it simple. You will do great.

extra_audio.text: Graziele presents the patient journey to a guest. First, the patient arrives at reception for the admission. Then, the nurse checks the patient. Next, the doctor asks for an exam in the laboratory. After that, the doctor reads the result. Finally, the patient goes home: this is the discharge.
